data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The fetch budget should be denominated in a composite unit 'fetch-credits' defined as max(requests, bytes/avg_bytes_per_request), with exhaustion recorded as a typed terminal state containing the credit balance and the formula parameters.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The formula is arbitrary and may not reflect actual resource costs; if the average bytes per request is misestimated, one dimension may be effectively unbounded.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The max operation can lead to premature exhaustion on one dimension while the other is underutilized, wasting budget.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"This approach is less transparent than separate counters, making auditing harder.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"This normalizes both dimensions into a single scalar, simplifying the budget check to one comparison. The formula uses a configurable average bytes per request to convert bytes into request-equivalent units, and takes the max to ensure both dimensions are bounded. Exhaustion occurs when credits reach zero. The terminal state includes the credit history and the formula, making it auditable.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
